previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mrs. ___ was admitted with abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and odynophagia, following a recent hospitalization for respiratory symptoms. She has a complex history including prior tracheal cancer treated with radiation, which likely contributed to esophageal stricture and ulceration. A barium swallow revealed a 3 cm esophageal stricture that prevented passage of a 12-mm tablet, and EGD confirmed severe radiation-related esophagitis with an ulcer and nodule, both biopsied. Due to inflammation, dilation was deferred. She was treated empirically for candidal esophagitis with fluconazole and started on high-dose pantoprazole. Her viral upper respiratory infection resolved with supportive care, and her abdominal symptoms improved with antiemetics and bowel management. Prednisone was adjusted for rheumatoid arthritis flare, and her asthma, heart failure, and hypertension were managed. She was discharged home with services on a prednisone taper, pantoprazole, fluconazole, and follow-up plans for biopsy results and GI reevaluation.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ female with breast cancer and non-small cell lung
cancer, both in remission, now more recently diagnosed with tracheal cancer
complicated by esophagitis, now with abdominal pain radiating up into the
chest.

STUDY:  AP and lateral chest radiograph.

COMPARISON:  ___ and chest CT from ___.

FINDINGS/IMPRESSION:  The heart size is borderline enlarged.  The mediastinal
contours are unremarkable.  The lung volumes are low with elevation of the
right hemidiaphragm and streaks of atelectasis or scarring.  There is no large
pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  Bilateral humeral head hemi-arthroplasties
are present.

CHEST CT, ___

HISTORY:  ___ woman with fever, cough and productive sputum.  On
prednisone.

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector helical scanning of the chest was coordinated with
intravenous infusion of 75 cc Omnipaque nonionic iodinated contrast agent
reconstructed as contiguous 5- and 1.25-mm thick axial and 5-mm thick coronal
and parasagittal images compared to chest CT scans since ___, most
recently CTA ___.

FINDINGS:

In addition to the brief clinical description provided, I understand that this
patient has a history of breast cancer, lung cancer, and tracheal cancer, with
radiation-induced esophagitis.

This history serves to explain the interval increase in both the ___ of
circumferential thickeing of the wall of the mid esophagus and the bulk of the
retrotracheal soft tissue at the level of the aortic arch.  It is difficult to
separate inflammatory thickening of the wall of the upper esophagus from tumor
infiltration, particularly since the tracheal lumen is now quite irregular
with a lateral projection, 2:12, that could be either a large ulcer or a
pseudodiverticulum due to scarring.  There is also an increase in soft tissue
bulk at the level of the carina where the spur is blunted, perhaps by local
tumor infiltration.  The ___ of the subcarinal soft tissue measured
from the posterior wall of the intrapericardial right pulmonary artery to the
vertebral body, and from the esophageal lumen to the right lung are 23 x 19
mm, previously 20 x 14 mm.  Again, it is difficult to separate esophageal
inflammation and reactive lymph nodes from malignant recurrence, but
thickening of the posterior wall of the right main bronchus, is also new.  A
16 x 14 mm right lower paratracheal lymph node, 2:14, is difficult to discern
on any prior CT scans, but may be new also.

Heart is mildly enlarged, unchanged.  There is no pericardial effusion.  Small
right pleural effusion has increased.  This study is not designed for
subdiaphragmatic diagnosis, but shows no adrenal mass.  It is not appropriate
for liver evaluation.

Radiation fibrosis in the paramediastinal left upper lobe, and subpleural
aspect of the right anterior lung are stable.  There is new mild peribronchial
opacification in the superior segment of the left lower lobe.  Given the
severe esophagitis and the possibility of tumor recurrence interfering with
swallowing, the most likely explanation for this is aspiration.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Severe wall thickening, mid esophagus, probably esophagitis.  Peritracheal
and peribronchial soft tissue thickening and increase in subcarinal right
lower paraesophageal lymph node size could also be radiation effect, but is
indistinguishable from recurrent infiltrating tumor.  Distortion of the lower
tracheal lumen could be due to scarring, but needs to be kept in mind as a
possible stricture or ulceration, in turn raising the possibility of a
recurrent tracheal carcinoma.

Findings were discussed by telephone with the resident physician caring for
this patient at the time of dictation.

including breast cancer, non-small cell lung cancer and tracheal cancer, now
status post XRT and chemo with complication with esophagitis, dysphagia and
odynophagia.  Please place G-tube.

RADIOLOGISTS:  Dr. ___ (resident), Dr. ___ (attending).  Dr.
___ attending radiologist, was present throughout the procedure.

SEDATION:  Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of
fentanyl and Versed throughout the total intra-service time of 1 hour 20

monitored.  75 mcg of fentanyl and 1 mg of Versed were used. 

PROCEDURE TECHNIQUE:  Signed informed written consent was obtained prior to
the procedure.  The patient was placed supine on the angiographic table.  An

was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  The liver edge was

Under fluoroscopic guidance, a site was selected overlying the anterior
abdominal wall corresponding to the stomach below.  Lateral fluoroscopic
images were obtained to ensure no overlying bowel.  The stomach continued to
be insufflated through an NG tube.  1% lidocaine was used for topical
anesthesia.  Three T-fasteners were deployed within the gastric lumen.  The
position was confirmed by injection of contrast and aspiration of air.  A
19-gauge needle was then advanced into the stomach until air was aspirated. 
Contrast was then injected to ensure correct positioning.  A ___ wire was
advanced through the 19-gauge needle and curled within the stomach as seen on
fluoroscopic images.  The needle was then exchanged for a dilator which was
subsequently exchanged for a 6 ___ sheath.  A Kumpe catheter was then
advanced through the sheath and directed towards the pylorus.  A Glidewire was
exchanged for the ___ wire and with subsequent manipulation we were able
to advance both the Kumpe and the Glidewire into the duodenum and subsequently
into the jejunum.  Contrast was then injected to ensure positioning within the
jejunum.  The ___ wire was exchanged for an Amplatz wire.  The sheath and
Kumpe catheter were then removed.  After successful dilations with a 12 ___
dilator, a 14 ___ peel-away sheath with dilator was introduced over the
Amplatz wire. The dilator was removed and over the Amplatz wire, the 14 ___
___ tube was then advanced with fluoroscopic guidance.  ___ tube tip was
seen within the jejunum and the Amplatz and peel-away sheath were subsequently
removed.  Contrast was then injected ensuring the placement within the
jejunum.  The loop was formed and locked.  The feeding tube was secured to the
skin using 0 silk sutures and a Flexi-Trak.  The site was dressed.  There were
no post-procedure complications.  The NG tube was removed.

IMPRESSION:  Successful placement of a 14 ___ ___ tube with tip
terminating in the jejunum.  No immediate complications.
